title: Structure Language Models for Protein Conformation Generation

nodes.text: Structure Language Modeling (SLM) is a framework for protein conformation generation that encodes 3D structures into a compact discrete latent space via a discrete VAE, then performs conditional language modeling over the structure tokens to capture sequence-specific conformation distributions.
nodes.evidence: we introduce Structure Language Modeling (SLM) as a novel framework for efficient protein conformation generation

nodes.text: ESMDiff is a BERT-like structure language model instantiation fine-tuned from ESM3 using masked discrete diffusion, grounded in the SLM framework.
nodes.evidence: we instantiate SLM with various popular LM architectures as well as proposing the ESMDiff, a novel BERT-like structure language model fine-tuned from ESM3 with masked diffusion

nodes.text: SLM training is a two-stage, separable EM-style pipeline: first jointly learn a dVAE encoder/decoder with a fixed uniform prior, then train the conditional prior over latent tokens via maximum likelihood (KL minimization), parameterized by language models (encoder-decoder like T5 or decoder-only like GPT).
nodes.evidence: we adopt an one-step expectation–maximization (EM) approach by first jointly learning pφ and qψ with a simple and parameter-free prior distribution p(z|c), followed by optimization on pθ

nodes.text: By generating in a discrete latent space, SLM bypasses the equivariant constraints of geometric symmetries required when modeling protein structures explicitly in 3D Euclidean space, and benefits from enhanced model capacity.
nodes.evidence: SLM bypasses the complexity of equivariant constraints associated with geometric symmetries and benefits from enhanced model capacity

nodes.text: Normalizing flow-based Boltzmann generators (Noe et al. 2019; Klein et al. 2023) struggle to scale to large proteins with hundreds of amino acids because the invertibility constraint obstructs scaling up model parameters.
nodes.evidence: normalizing flow-based methods... face significant challenges in modeling large protein systems with hundreds of amino acids, as the invertibility constraint becomes a major obstacle

nodes.text: L2-based denoising score matching objectives tend to predict local perturbations rather than remote alternative-conformation modes, causing diffusion models to overallocate capacity to structural noise instead of low-frequency structural changes.
nodes.evidence: L2-based training objectives such as denoising score matching tend to predict local perturbations rather than capturing remote modes of alternative conformations

nodes.text: Existing deep conformation samplers (EigenFold, Str2Str, AlphaFlow, ConfDiff, DiG) predominantly rely on diffusion or flow matching in 3D geometric space, which centers around metastable states and is runtime-inefficient.
nodes.evidence: these methods predominantly rely on the diffusion process within a 3D geometric space, which typically centers around the vicinity of metastable states and is often inefficient in terms of runtime

nodes.text: Structure prediction models such as AlphaFold2 and RosettaFold predict static structures but often fail to capture the dynamic, multi-conformation nature of proteins.
nodes.evidence: yet often fail to accurately capture the dynamic nature of proteins and their multiple conformations

nodes.text: ESMDiff treats discrete diffusion as interpolation between categorical distributions: with an explicit stationary distribution, a state-independent transition kernel makes the forward marginal a controlled interpolation between the data token and the stationary distribution governed by a monotone schedule alpha(t).
nodes.evidence: the discrete diffusion, when defined with an explicit stationary distribution, can be viewed as an interpolation between two categorical distributions controlled by α(t)

nodes.text: SLM achieves a 20-100x speedup over existing generative methods in generating diverse conformations, with reported state-of-the-art performance.
nodes.evidence: offering a 20-100x speedup than existing methods in generating diverse conformations

nodes.text: SLM/ESMDiff was validated across multiple scenarios including BPTI equilibrium dynamics, conformational change pairs, and intrinsically disordered proteins.
nodes.evidence: We verify our approach in various scenarios, including the equilibrium dynamics of BPTI, conformational change pairs, and intrinsically disordered proteins

nodes.text: The discrete latent encoding removes high-frequency structural details to form 'structure languages' that capture the uncertainty of complex conformations, with residue flexibility reflected by the categorical distribution over latent tokens.
nodes.evidence: The discrete latent encoding removes high-frequency details of protein structures, forming "structure languages" that effectively capture the uncertainty of complex protein conformations
